title: Audio upload from the Afriklang app to Sayari (campaign recordings)

request.auth: X-Upload-Key header, added by the app's server-side proxy (/api/audio-upload). The browser never holds it.
notes: All fields are multipart text parts; the audio is the 'files' part. Numbers are sent as decimal strings (for example "8.2").
Absent values are left out, never sent empty.
Fields marked campaign_only are sent for campaign recordings only; the older learning-app upload sends the first six fields and nothing else.
No name, email, phone number or account id is ever sent. The speaker_id is the only identity.

files.description: The recording: WAV, PCM 16-bit, 16 kHz, mono. One file per request. Never re-encoded after capture, so its sha-256 equals source_sha256.

language.description: ISO 639-3 code of the campaign's language.

consent_recorded.description: Always "true" for a campaign: the app does not let anyone record before the account and campaign consents are signed.

dialect.description: The variety the contributor declared in their profile.

english_description.example: Ask your bank how to check your mobile money balance.
english_description.description: The prompt the contributor was shown (the sentence to read, or the topic or scenario). Ground truth for read speech.

speaker_id.description: Pseudonymous speaker ID, created on the contributor's first profile save and never changed. Always present for campaign recordings.

campaign_code.description: Human-readable campaign code. Use it to look up the campaign's pre-annotation settings and delivery rules.

mission_id.description: Dashboard's mission id (one mission = one prompt for one contributor).

mission_type.description: Speech type. Drives the transcription type and, for conversations, how the channels are read.

prompt_id.description: The prompt the mission was generated from.

prompt_category.description: The prompt's category, when the campaign defines one.

partner_speaker_id.description: Conversational missions only: the other speaker. One device records both, so both speaker IDs belong to this one file.

source_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the uploaded file. The dashboard uses it to recognise a retried upload; Sayari can use it to refuse a duplicate.

sample_rate.description: Hz, as measured on the file.

channels.description: Always 1 today (two-device capture is not supported).

level_dbfs.description: Average level in dBFS (0 is full scale; the campaign refuses anything quieter than its minimum, usually -35).

peak_dbfs.description: Peak level in dBFS. 0 or above means clipped (the app refuses those takes before upload).

silence_before_s.description: Silence before the first speech, seconds.

silence_after_s.description: Silence after the last speech, seconds.

device.description: Operating system and browser of the recording phone (coarse, from the user agent).

example_request_fields.english_description: Ask your bank how to check your mobile money balance.

body.audio_id: string, Sayari's id for the recording

notes: The app accepts audio_id, id or recording_id (also inside files/results/items/data/uploaded) and forwards it to the dashboard as sayari_recording_id. A missing id is tolerated.

The app never retries an upload by itself; an error shows a message and the contributor taps again. The dashboard answers a repeated source_sha256 with duplicate: true, so Sayari should accept or refuse a repeated source_sha256 consistently.
Error statuses the app understands: 413 too large, 429 rate limited, 5xx server, 4xx refused.

not_sent_by_the_app_decide_with_dashboar.campaign_settings: Pre-annotation settings (asr_model, language_code, vad_filter, condition_on_previous_text, low_conf_threshold, timestamps), annotation settings (transcription_type, tags, double_annotation_share, review_share, guideline_version) and quality thresholds live in the dashboard's campaign spec. The browser must not be the source of them. Proposal: Sayari looks them up by campaign_code, or the app's server-side proxy adds them.
not_sent_by_the_app_decide_with_dashboar.recording_status_back_to_dashboard: uploaded, pre_annotated, accepted or rejected (with a reason) is shown to contributors. The dashboard has the service function applyRecordingStatus but no HTTP route yet; Sayari's way of reporting it is not settled.
not_sent_by_the_app_decide_with_dashboar.pre_annotation_tests: The 5 pre-annotation tests are entered by hand by an admin on the campaign page; nothing flows from Sayari for them.
